newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds hold steady to Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds hold steady to Treasuries.

text.p: A stack of Ginnie Mae paper traded hands on Wednesday, inspiring an otherwise quiet U.S. mortgage-backed securities market, traders said.
"At one point during the day, there were about $150 million of Ginnie 8.0s trading on the screens, which were bid very aggressively," said one trader.
Another trader said he had heard of cross-market activity between Ginnie Maes and corporate bonds.
Pass-throughs were off 1/32 to 4/32 overall by late afternoon, with 30-year Ginnie Mae 8.0 percent coupons off 3/32 at 101-13/32.

In other key coupons, 30-year Ginnie 7.5s had slipped 2/32 to 99-12/32, yielding 111 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable FNMAs were off 3/32 at 99-09/32, and FHLMCs were down 3/32 at 99-14/32.
Spreads over Treasuries held steady to slightly narrower.
Government securities slid moderately lower after picking up rate-hike vibes from a speech by Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey, fixed-income analysts said.
Speaking at a conference sponsored by the Dallas Fed, Lindsey asserted the central bank's commitment to keeping a lid on inflation.
